solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Youngster is foremost in modernist art movement

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a young scout

indicators.note: the foremost letter of the word modernist is the one taken

explanation.surface: A young person is at the forefront of a modernist art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modernist art movement' looks like the whole definition, but 'modernist' is only there for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism is the early twentieth-century painting style of Picasso and Braque, an example of an art movement.

clue.text: Bird dog like pig

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
as means like, in the same way
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone describes a dog as looking like a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The curassow is a large turkey-like game bird of Central and South American forests.

clue.text: Running through marshy area, almost catching fish?

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bayou is a marshy creek or swamp, as in Louisiana
netting is catching fish with a net; the question mark flags the loose definition

explanation.surface: Someone running through a swamp nearly catches some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayonetting someone is stabbing them with a bayonet, i.e. running them through.

clue.text: Only Aretha Franklin's music is heard

indicators.note: is heard says the word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Aretha Franklin was the Queen of Soul, so her music is soul

explanation.surface: Aretha Franklin's music is the only thing to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means one and only, a direct synonym of only as an adjective.

clue.text: Go forward and go back, meeting resistance in crowd

indicators.note: in says the resistance-and-reversed piece goes inside the word for crowd

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd or throng
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: back says the second word go is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A struggle to advance and retreat against resistance within a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To progress is to move onward or advance, a verb synonym of going forward.

clue.text: Swedes, for example, introducing credit to poor vagrant

indicators.note: introducing says the credit abbreviation is put into the middle of the rearranged letters
vagrant means wandering, so the letters of to and poor wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: Swedish people offering credit to a poor homeless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedes' looks like people from Sweden, but a swede is a turnip-like vegetable (rutabaga). 'Vagrant' rearranges the fodder into ROOTOP, and 'introducing' sets the credit abbreviation into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A swede (rutabaga) is a vegetable grown for its edible swollen root, so it is an example of a root crop.

clue.text: Screw it in lug-'ole — means of ending debate

indicators.note: to screw something is to twist it, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; lug-'ole is British slang for ear

explanation.surface: A coarse instruction to shove something in your ear, as a way to end an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug-'ole' is British slang for an ear (lughole).
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament a guillotine is a timetable motion that cuts off debate on a bill, so it is a device for ending discussion.

clue.text: Scoff when leader is knocked out in preliminary round

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is knocked out, i.e. removed

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round of a race or contest

explanation.surface: A competitor gorges after the front-runner goes out in the qualifiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat greedily, so the two are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Cruel behaviour is accepted by deplorable male

indicators.note: accepted by says the word is goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: sad can mean pathetic or deplorable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cruel behaviour is tolerated by a contemptible man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is taking pleasure in inflicting pain on others, a form of cruel behaviour.

clue.text: Popular musician taking part in Normandy landings

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pop star taking part in the D-Day invasion of 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is a famous singer-songwriter, an example of a popular musician.

clue.text: Payment that isn't common

definitions.meaning: a sum paid to an author or patent holder for each sale
commoners are ordinary people; royals are by definition not common

explanation.definitionFit: Royalty means both a fee paid per copy sold and the class of kings and queens, who are not commoners.

clue.text: In a dictionary Romney is not mentioned

indicators.note: In says the first name goes inside the dictionary abbreviation

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Mitt Romney is the American politician, 2012 Republican presidential candidate

explanation.surface: A politician's name fails to appear in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been left out, i.e. not mentioned.

clue.text: Decline and fall from grace with king

parts.note: a sin is a moral lapse, a fall from grace
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: The decline and fall of a monarch who has sinned.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink is to go down or deteriorate, a verb synonym of decline.

clue.text: Old-fashioned guns are as good as security devices

parts.note: something that is a match for another is as good as it
locks are devices that keep things secure

explanation.surface: Antique firearms are claimed to be as effective as locks for keeping things safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchlock is an early musket fired by a slow match, an obsolete type of gun.

clue.text: Engineer on pitch with rare bat

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or construct it, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: an engineer works on the pitch with an unusual bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' and 'bat' suggest cricket, but the bat is the flying mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiroptera is the order of mammals comprising bats, so a chiropteran is a bat.

clue.text: Uncomfortably hot? Not a winter's gale, perhaps

indicators.note: Not says the letter a is left out of the pool before rearranging
perhaps signals that the remaining letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the letter removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A winter storm is hardly something that would leave you feeling too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The ? marks the definition as a description and also hints at the paradox of a winter gale being sweltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweltering describes oppressive heat that makes one sweat, so it means uncomfortably hot.

clue.text: Old engineer, retired, beginning to acquire capital

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the engineer's name is read backwards

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of acquire is used

explanation.surface: A veteran engineer, now retired, starts to buy some capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Toe? So it may be

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters can be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A doubtful look at a toe: yes, perhaps it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is its own definition: the letters of TOE SO IT rearranged give a word that is itself baby talk for a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is a childish or affectionate word for a foot or toe.

clue.text: Not much money for bread — nicker oddly enough

parts.note: pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread

indicators.note: oddly says the odd-numbered letters of nicker are kept

explanation.surface: A tiny sum paid for bread, which is strange given the price of a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicker' is British slang for a pound sterling, which helps the money surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small or inadequate amount of money.

clue.text: What Gershwin did is cool

definitions.meaning: George Gershwin wrote music, i.e. he created musical works

explanation.definitionFit: Composed is both the past tense of writing music and an adjective meaning calm and unruffled.

clue.text: House with a shed — one for German feudal tenant

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so the letter a is dropped

parts.note: a villa is a large country or suburban house
taken as written, the letter removed
ein is the German word for one

explanation.surface: A dwelling with a garden shed, one fit for a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like an outbuilding, but it is a verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A villein was a medieval serf bound to his lord's land, a type of feudal tenant.

clue.text: Altogether at home with Dorothy's dog

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Dorothy's dog stays home with everyone together.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for in total, a phrase meaning altogether or completely.

clue.text: Girl meets boy — and ducks

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
Des is a boy's name, short for Desmond

explanation.surface: A girl meets a boy, and they feed the ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' looks like the birds, but it is a verb meaning dodges.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge it, so ducks and evades are verb synonyms.

clue.text: A foursome for bridge with no wear and tear

parts.note: the four players at bridge are named by compass points: South, North, East, West

explanation.surface: A bridge four plays without causing any damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as new shows no signs of use, the same condition as fresh from the shop.

clue.text: Vet sitting mongrel in drawer?

indicators.note: a mongrel is a mixed breed, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet is sitting with a mongrel inside a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture, but is one who draws; the ? flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignettist is an artist who makes vignettes, small decorative drawings, so one kind of drawer in the sense of draughtsman.

clue.text: Action taken when backing favourites

indicators.note: backing says the word for favourites is read in reverse

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A gambler makes a move when betting on the favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests betting on horses, but it is the reversal indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure or action taken, as in taking steps to fix a problem.

clue.text: Fancy one almost pushing up the daisies

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pushing up the daisies is an idiom for being dead and buried

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a person who is nearly dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim, a noun synonym of a thought or plan.

clue.text: Dissatisfaction with loss of filling, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: loss of filling says the word's middle letters are removed, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: Unhappiness at losing a tooth filling affects the way one talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss of filling' removes SSATISFA from the middle of DISSATISFACTION, leaving DI and CTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a person's style of enunciation, i.e. their way of speaking.

clue.text: Group of workers reported in vineyard

indicators.note: reported says the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a crew is a team of people working together

explanation.surface: A team of labourers is said to be at the vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cru is French for a vineyard or wine-growing estate of recognised quality.

clue.text: Bears stop by river and start to swim

parts.note: an end is a stop or finish
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: start to says only the first letter of swim is taken

explanation.surface: Bears halt beside a river and begin to swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like animals, but it is a verb meaning tolerates.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it, so bears and the answer are synonyms meaning tolerates.

clue.text: Runner more complacent about tail end

indicators.note: about says the comparative goes around the letter from tail

parts.note: smugger means more self-satisfied

indicators.note: end says the final letter of tail is taken

explanation.surface: A rather too pleased athlete fusses about the back of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is one who runs contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is someone who smuggles goods, as in gun-runner or rum-runner.

clue.text: Page a Brontë daughter pulled to pieces

parts.note: Anne Brontë was the youngest of the novelist sisters

explanation.surface: A critic savages a page by one of the Brontë sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan something is to criticise it severely, so panned means harshly criticised.
